axes.model_access:
It calls no model itself; it is an interface implementation called by clients.
Its core is converting web-page HTML into Markdown for LLM consumption.
axes.runtime:
A local **Python** process communicating over stdio.
It depends on the Python MCP SDK 1.x (requires mcp>=1.29.0,<2); SDK 2.0 renamed the APIs this server uses.

A 2026-08-30 fix addressed security and compatibility issues of container bind mounts under Docker / Podman / SELinux.
axes.local_files: **No file read/write tools.** The core capability is web fetching; local files are not involved.
axes.background: Not supported. A single fetch is a synchronous operation, ending with the client process.
axes.tools:
It provides the fetch tool to retrieve web content and convert it to Markdown.
Output is converted text; **its degree of structure depends on the target page itself**.
axes.context: Stateless. Each call is independent; no fetch history is kept.
axes.permissions:
**The official docs warn explicitly about the security risk**: the README states this server
**can access local/internal IP addresses and may represent a security risk**.
Use with caution and make sure no sensitive data is exposed.
There is no separate approval mechanism, and the target-address range cannot be restricted.
axes.fit:
Converts public web content to Markdown for an Agent to read.
**Not a fit for environments with intranet access**,
nor for pages requiring login state.

mcp.transport:
Supports stdio, **and offers container deployment (Docker / Podman)**.
The 2026-08-30 fix addressed bind-mount security and compatibility (including SELinux).

The official README (full-text verification 2026-10-08) gives only local-process integration:
uvx / pip / Docker; there is no official launch method for a remote transport.
mcp.auth:
No separate authentication layer. In stdio form it inherits the client user's permissions.
**Authentication configuration for the container form is not stated in the repo.**
mcp.scope:
**The highest-risk class**: no file scope (files are not involved),
but **the network range cannot be narrowed** —
the official warning says it can access local/internal IPs.
No address allowlist, no approval mechanism.
An assessment is mandatory before using it in production or in environments hosting intranet services.

sectionTitles.为什么这个风险值得单独说: Why this risk deserves its own section

sections.⚠ 官方安全警告（原文）:
> **CAUTION**
> This server can access local/internal IP addresses and may represent a security risk.
> Exercise caution when using this MCP server to ensure this does not expose any sensitive data.

**This is the clearest self-flagged risk by the official side in this entire section**,
and the site considers it the most valuable first-hand information — such warnings are rare;
most comparable tools only write "be careful when using".
sections.为什么这个风险值得单独说:
| Scenario | Risk |
|---|---|
| Intranet has database admin panels (`10.x` / `192.168.x`) | The Agent may fetch intranet pages |
| Cloud metadata services (e.g. `169.254.169.254`) | Instance metadata and credentials may be obtained |
| A dev server runs on the local machine | Local service responses may be fetched |
| The Agent is lured into fetching a malicious URL | Intranet topology can be probed |

**The key point**: there is no address allowlist and no approval mechanism.
Once enabled, the Agent has a channel for probing the intranet.
sections.变更记录说明:
**This object has no standalone changelog page**; change records are in the directory's commit history:

| Date | Content |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-30 | Fix container bind-mount security and compatibility (Docker / Podman / SELinux) |
| 2026-08-18 | Document the Python MCP 1.x version requirement |
| 2026-08-18 | Pin the dependency `mcp>=1.29.0,<2` |
| 2026-07-29 | Batch uv dependency updates |

**Two entries worth noting**:

- **The 08-18 version pin**: SDK 2.0 renamed the APIs this server uses, and the official side pins it to 1.x.
  If your environment has SDK 2.x installed, this server may fail to start.

- **The 08-30 container fix** is the same commit (#2205) as git / time, showing these three servers shared a containerization problem.
sections.输出质量评估:
**Output structure depends on the target page itself**; there is no unified schema:

| Target page type | Output quality |
|---|---|
| Documentation sites (regular structure) | good |
| Blog article bodies | medium |
| Single-page apps (content rendered by JS) | **poor** — the body text cannot be fetched |
| Pages requiring login | **fails** |
| Pure images / PDFs | unusable |

**This is not a defect of the server, but it defines the tool's applicability boundary.**
sections.部署建议:
If you really need it, consider it only under these conditions:

| Condition | Explanation |
|---|---|
| Isolated network environment | not on the same segment as intranet services |
| or containerized with egress restricted | allowlist outbound, only target domains permitted |
| and no intranet-access requirement is accepted | because it cannot be restricted |

**Note**: containerization alone does not solve this risk —
inside a container the host network is still reachable unless network policies are configured.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement**: measurement of this server **should not be done in environments containing sensitive intranet services**.
Verify fetch success rate and output quality in an isolated container or test network.
